# OptChat: an endless chat where the AI remembers everything

## What this is

AI agents forget. A chat session fills up, gets compacted or thrown away, and the next one starts from zero. If you work with agents every day, your life ends up scattered over hundreds of sessions in different tools, and the agent can't find any of it: not the decision you made last month, not the algorithm you designed in March, not the PR you forgot to answer.

Long sessions have a second problem: context rot . The longer the context, the worse the model works. Compaction ("summarize and keep going") throws detail away for good, and the result keeps decaying.

OptChat fixes both with one idea: the chat history itself is the memory , stored as a compressed tree.

- There is ONE chat, and it never ends. Every message (yours, the agent's replies, its tool calls and their results) is appended to a log and kept forever, word for word.

- In the background, a cheap model compresses the log into a binary tree of one-line summaries: each message becomes a line, two adjacent lines merge into one line covering both, two of those merge again, and so on.

- Each time you send a message, the agent starts FRESH: no leftover context. It sees a fixed-size "view" (about 64k tokens) of the WHOLE chat: recent messages one line each, older ones many per line, the older the coarser. Then it sees your message.

- When a line is too vague, the agent "zooms": it opens the line into the two lines it was made from, down to the original message. Any fact from your whole history is a few zooms away.

What you get:

- Infinite context with a constant size. Nothing is ever deleted; only the resolution of the distant past fades.

- No context rot and no manual compaction. Every turn starts clean.

- Low cost. Most tokens of an agent turn are its own tool loop, and that is prompt-cached. Across turns, the view changes only near its end, so most of it is cached too.

- Your instructions stick. Corrections and preferences you give in chat stay in the memory (the compressor ranks your own words first), so most of an AGENTS.md becomes unnecessary: change your mind in a message and the latest ruling wins.

- You can browse it too. The tree is a plain file you can walk from the root down to any message.

OptChat grew out of OptMem (github.com/VictorTaelin/OptMem), a memory tool: an append-only log of short notes plus a summary tree, which an agent reads at the start of each session. OptChat turns that around: instead of a tool the agent calls, the memory IS the chat, and the harness builds every turn from it.

The rest of this document is a complete technical spec, for anyone (human or AI) who wants to build it. It describes a working implementation in full, including the reasons behind each choice. Many choices that look natural are wrong (they break the cache, or make the memory decay, or make the agent act on partial text), and the spec says which and why. If you are an AI building this: follow it exactly, and when you deviate, have a reason that the spec does not already refute.

# Technical specification

## 1. Overview

Components:

- The log (ROOT): every message, verbatim, append-only.

- The tree : summaries. Node (l, i) covers messages [i·2^l, (i+1)·2^l) . Level 0 summarizes one message; level l > 0 merges its two children (l-1, 2i) and (l-1, 2i+1) .

- The compactor : a background worker that builds tree nodes with a cheap model, in a strict order.

- The view : a list of tree nodes that covers the whole chat, oldest first, kept under a byte budget, changed incrementally.

- The turn loop : each user message starts a fresh model call whose input is [system prompt] [view] [new message] , plus tools zoom and date .

- Caching : the request layout and cache breakpoints that make all of this cheap.

Constants used in the reference implementation:

All sizes are UTF-8 bytes (or characters, for the cache marks), never tokens: a tokenizer changes between models, a byte count never does.

## 2. Storage

Two append-only streams in one directory:

chat/ main/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl one message per line: {i, kind, text, size, date} tree/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl one node per line: {l, i, text, size}

- i is the message index (0, 1, 2, ...), its permanent id. kind is one of: user (the user's words; also subagent reports, see §9), talk (the agent's replies), tool (the agent's tool calls, as text: name and JSON input), echo (tool results), note (memories imported from an older system). date is ISO time. size = bytes of kind + ": " + text .

- A line goes to the file of the local day it was written. Files split by day only to keep them manageable; the ids are global.

- Durability : each line is written with one write and then fsync , before the function returns. A crash loses nothing written.

- Torn lines : at load, a line that is not valid JSON (a crash mid-write) is reported and skipped, and a file not ending in \n gets one appended, so the next write starts on its own line.

- One writer : two processes on the same chat would corrupt it. Hold a lock for the life of the process. The reference uses a Unix socket: the process listens on lock ; a second process that can connect to it exits; a socket that refuses connections is stale (the OS frees it when the owner dies), so it is deleted and taken over. No PID files, no timeouts.

- The tree is a cache in principle (rebuildable from the log), but it costs model calls to rebuild, so it is stored and never recomputed.

Never edit or delete anything in these files. The log is history.

Thoughts (model reasoning) are shown to the user but never logged . Reason: the compactor would have to summarize them, and Claude Sonnet's reasoning-extraction safeguard refused the compactor on thoughts in 112 of 630 first tries; without thoughts, 0 of 523. Thoughts also add little that the replies and tool calls don't already show.

## 3. The tree

node(0, i) = message i, in ≤ NODE bytes node(l, i) = merge(node(l-1, 2i), node(l-1, 2i+1)), in ≤ NODE bytes covers(l,i) = messages [i·2^l, (i+1)·2^l)

The tree is purely binary . (OptMem built small blocks of up to 16 memories straight from the raw notes, and only bigger ones from two halves. That had no real justification and made the structure confusing; OptChat dropped it. Every parent comes from exactly its two children.)

Free nodes. If the source already fits in NODE bytes, it IS the node, with no model call:

- level 0: kind + ": " + text of a short message, verbatim (so short user messages stay word for word forever, up to the level where they get merged);

- level > 0: childA + "\n" + childB , if that fits.

Why 512 bytes. It started at 128 and the model couldn't write useful lines that short (and overshot often). OptMem used 280. 512 bytes is a dense paragraph: room for several items with names and numbers. With an average real line around 250 bytes, a 128 KB view holds ~500 lines.

Addressing. A node is named id+n : id = its first message, n = 2^l = how many messages it covers. So node(l, i) is (i·2^l)+(2^l) . Real message ids, not tree coordinates: the agent reads 2184+8 in the view and calls zoom(2184, 8) directly.

## 4. The compactor

### 4.1 When a node is built

A background loop ("pump") scans all levels and starts every node that:

- is not built and not already running;

- has its sources: level 0, the message exists; level > 0, both children are built;

- has its whole context summarized: every line of the current view that lies before the node's end is a built summary (see the first function below).

Up to JOBS run at once. After each finishes (or fails), pump again.

Rule 3 is essential, and it gives OptMem's order for free: messages are compressed one at a time, in order , while merges of finished parts run alongside. The compactor never sees a line that isn't a summary.

function first(mem): # first message whose view line is unbuilt for part in mem.view: if not built(part): return start(part) return len(mem.root) function pump(mem): T = len(mem.root) for l = 0 while 2^l <= T: for i = 0 while (i+1)·2^l <= T: if len(busy) >= JOBS: return end = (l == 0) ? i : (i+1)·2^l if built(l,i) or busy(l,i) or not ready(l,i) or end > first(mem): continue busy.add((l,i)) build(l,i).then( ok -> busy.remove((l,i)); fail.remove((l,i)); pump(mem), err -> report err once per node; after RETRY: busy.remove((l,i)); pump(mem))

For level 0 node i , end = i means "every view line before message i is a summary", so node i is the first unbuilt one. For a merge, end = (i+1)·2^l means everything up to the node's last message is summarized.

Retry : a failed node waits RETRY (10 s) and is tried again, forever; only its first failure is reported. Don't use long exponential backoff: the next turn waits for these summaries (§6), so the compactor must catch up as fast as possible.

### 4.2 What a compactor call sees

One call per node, with no tools, on a cheap model (the reference uses Claude Sonnet at medium effort; at low effort it overshot the size limit much more). Input:

- system : the COMPACT prompt (§4.4), constant.

- user message , two text blocks: Context : the current view's lines up to the node, wrapped in <chat> ... </chat> . For a level-0 node: lines covering messages before it (the message itself comes whole in block 2). For a merge: lines up to the node's last message. The step : For scale, this line is exactly 512 bytes: <SCALE: a realistic summary line of exactly 512 bytes> Compress this message into one line, in at most 512 bytes: <kind>: <the message, whole, newlines kept> or, for a merge: For scale, this line is exactly 512 bytes: <SCALE> Merge these two lines into one, in at most 512 bytes: <child A text, newlines flattened to spaces> <child B text, newlines flattened to spaces>

Why each piece:

- The context block. The first version gave the compactor only the message (or the two lines) and nothing else. A summarizer that doesn't know what's going on writes useless summaries: it can't resolve "do it", "the other one", "that file". With the view, it knows the project, the people, the open question, and can even recover detail its input lost. It is ~64k tokens per call, but it is the same prefix across calls, so put it first and let it cache.

- NO IDS anywhere in a compactor call. View lines are shown bare (text only, one per line), and the step's lines too. When lines were shown as id+n|text , the model copied the format and began its own output with an id (6 of 16 tries on one big message). Without ids: 0 of 32. The <chat> lines have no markers at all, and the two lines to merge are written out again, whole, under the instruction, so the model never has to "find" them.

- SCALE. Models can't count bytes. A real example line of exactly NODE bytes gives them a sense of the size. Use a realistic, dense, multi-item line, tagged with kinds like a real summary.

# Claude Code burns ~15–20% of your tokens on a 3-word status line. Here's how to turn it off

by Flamerix AI · MIT License

> Tested on Linux, Claude Code 2.1.257–2.1.312 (see Tested versions). The binary is not modified ( BUN_OPTIONS=--preload ). An update can silently undo it, so see Verify.

## TL;DR

curl -fsSL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/flamerix-ai/c3905705cc4205e5de3011fa2e74efce/raw/no-agent-summary.js -o ~ /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js claude daemon stop --any BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload $HOME /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js " claude

To make it permanent for every Claude Code process, see Install .

## The problem

Every ~30 seconds, for every background agent, Claude Code sends that agent's entire transcript to the agent's own model (usually Opus) and asks it to "describe your most recent action in 3-5 words". The answer only updates the agent's status line in the agents panel; it never reaches the model or your conversation. There is no setting that turns it off, and since 2.1.232 (August 2026) it has been on by default.

The anomaly was detected by DRIM in Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export: grouping claude_code.api_request events by query_source showed agent_summary costing more than the main conversation itself .

Spend here means Claude Code's own per-request estimate ( cost_usd ), not an invoice: on a subscription, what you lose is rate-limit headroom. We are not the only ones who measured it: #86879 collects four independent measurements of 18–26 %.

## The fix (how it works)

no-agent-summary.js is a Bun preload (~80 lines of code). It wraps setTimeout / setInterval ; when a callback's source text contains a summarizer anchor (e.g. the [AgentSummary] Timer fired log line), it returns an inert handle instead of arming the timer. Every other timer passes through untouched. In the OpenTelemetry export the suppressed requests are claude_code.api_request events with query_source = agent_summary .

Why a timer hook rather than something simpler: the module ships as precompiled Bun bytecode, so editing its JS text inside the binary changes nothing, and the API client does not go through a wrapped globalThis.fetch . But Function.prototype.toString still returns a callback's source even when it runs from bytecode, so the timer can be recognised by a string inside it. The inert timer uses exactly 2³¹−1 ms: Node and Bun treat a larger delay as 1 ms, so an "infinite" delay would fire at once.

## Install

- Put no-agent-summary.js somewhere stable; note its absolute path.

- Set BUN_OPTIONS globally so every Claude Code process gets it. One of: # ~/.profile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc export BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js " # ~/.config/fish/config.fish set -gx BUN_OPTIONS " --preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js " # ~/.config/environment.d/50-no-agent-summary.conf (systemd user env; also reaches # user services and timers; applies when the user manager next starts, usually next login) BUN_OPTIONS =--preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js Or a wrapper named claude earlier on PATH (the case keeps it idempotent when one Claude Code process starts another): #! /bin/sh HOOK=/abs/path/no-agent-summary.js case " ${BUN_OPTIONS-} " in * " --preload $HOOK " * ) ;; * ) export BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload $HOOK " ;; esac : " ${CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG := ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR :-/ tmp} / no-agent-summary.log} " export CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG exec /path/to/the/real/claude " $@ "

### Env

## Nuances

- Restart the daemon after install. The daemon, pty host and pre-warmed bg-spare sessions inherit the environment of the client that started the daemon, so a daemon started before BUN_OPTIONS was set keeps spawning unhooked sessions. Hence claude daemon stop --any .

- Headless runs need it too: claude -p , cron, CI, editor integrations.

- Platform: Linux tested, macOS and Windows untested. On Windows the /$bunfs/ gate most likely never installs the hook.

- A/B: CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_MODE=pass loads the hook but arms every timer; the summaries come back, which shows the off result is the hook's doing.

- Background processes: daemon, pty host and bg-spare must carry --preload in their environment ( /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux); if not, restart the daemon.

## Verify (after every update)

- Preload loads: BUN_OPTIONS= " --preload $HOME /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js " CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG=/tmp/nas.log claude --version && cat /tmp/nas.log Expect preload active mode=off … . No line: BUN_OPTIONS did not reach the process, or the path is not absolute.

Preload loads:

BUN_OPTIONS= " --preload $HOME /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js " CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG=/tmp/nas.log claude --version && cat /tmp/nas.log

Expect preload active mode=off … . No line: BUN_OPTIONS did not reach the process, or the path is not absolute.

- Timer suppressed: with the same BUN_OPTIONS and CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG=/tmp/nas.log , run a background subagent for a minute or two. The log shows summary timer #1 suppressed (setTimeout, delay=30000) and the agent's panel status stops updating. If you export OpenTelemetry, query_source = agent_summary should stay at zero; this is the only check that catches every failure mode.

### Fail-open

Matching is by source text : an anchor must sit inside the callback passed to the timer. If an update breaks that, the hook matches nothing and summaries silently come back. Ways it can happen:

- the log line or query-source id is renamed;

- the callback is passed via fn.bind(...) (no source in toString ) or another wrapper;

- the strings move to a shared constant outside the callback;

- the timer moves to an unwrapped API ( timers/promises , a scheduler loop).

So re-run Verify after every update.

## Effect

- We run it under every Claude Code process on our machine (2.1.301). Since then there have been zero agent_summary requests, and no other side query grew to take its place.

- Subagents, background agents, forked skills and background sessions run normally; only the summary fork is skipped.

- Visible change: the per-agent panel status stops updating; SDK task_progress has no summary .

- Overhead: one Function.prototype.toString per distinct timer callback, cached in a WeakMap . claude --version : ~10 ms → ~17 ms (one measurement).

## Tested versions

Linux x64 binary from npm @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64 (its sha256 equals the native installer's manifest.json checksum). Static: the extracted bundle's summary timer callback carries a hook anchor. Live: claude -p --model haiku with CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES=1 , one subagent doing 8 steps of ~20 s, counting [AgentSummary] Forking in --debug-file .

5 / 5 / 0 = the fork happens on this version, merely loading the hook changes nothing, and off removes it.

## Why there is no setting for this

- The documented switch only turns it on. The SDK option agentProgressSummaries defaults to false , but in the bundle it is one term of an OR, and every code path that writes it sets true . So false changes nothing, and the undocumented CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES can only enable summaries too.

- The interval belongs to the server. It comes from a per-model-family server flag and is clamped to 30–240 s. The default is already the minimum, and no value disables the timer.

- The obvious env vars miss. DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS , which some packagers set, does not occur in the binary at all. CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 do stop it, but only by taking fork subagents or background agents with it.

- The prompt cache makes it cheaper, not cheap. About 98 % of these calls re-read the transcript from cache; the ~2 % that hit a cold cache carry over a third of its cost.

- Cost tools that read transcripts don't see it. These requests are not written to the session logs on disk ( #104358 ); only the OpenTelemetry export shows them. The docs section on background token usage doesn't list it either, while Agent View's row summaries are documented as a Haiku-class model refreshing every few minutes.

- A cheaper variant already exists, switched off. 2.1.310 ships a short mode: about 2k tokens of notes instead of the full transcript, optionally written by a smaller model. The default is still the full transcript, and only server flags can change it.

### Timeline (2026)

In our telemetry its weekly share of spend went from 3.5–7 % in July (the fork gate was already open for us) to 7.3 % and then 11.8 % in the week we picked up 2.1.233, and to about 16 % by mid-October.
